project.title: Wireless microphone mod for ON M45 speaker
project.objective: Identify and prove a usable audio interface inside the wireless karaoke microphone, then reproduce intelligible microphone audio through the ON M45 AUX input without modifying the speaker.
iteration_exit_criteria: Major microphone functional blocks are documented well enough to explain the signal path.
At least one usable audio interface is identified and electrically characterized.
Microphone audio is reproduced intelligibly through the ON M45 AUX input.
The effect of microphone controls/DSP on the chosen interface is understood.
There is enough evidence to select the Iteration 2 wireless architecture.
out_of_scope_for_iteration: Battery integration for a replacement transmitter
Full reverse engineering of the existing RF protocol
Permanent modification of the ON M45 speaker

nodes.title: RF discovery conclusion
nodes.summary: The microphone is a confirmed 2.4 GHz transmitter. Its activity is state-correlated and distributed across separated parts of the 2.4 GHz ISM band. It does not appear as an ordinary pairable Bluetooth audio device. Exact protocol remains unresolved and is not the Iteration 1 critical path.

nodes.title: Speaker-side constraint
nodes.summary: The ON M45 already provides a 3.5 mm AUX input, so Iteration 1 should treat the speaker as a solved analog output endpoint and avoid opening or modifying it.

nodes.title: Iteration 1 architectural principle
nodes.summary: Do not make RF protocol decoding the main task. Find the latest practical audio interface before wireless transmission: prefer post-DSP analog, then processed digital audio, then pre-DSP/raw microphone audio.

nodes.title: Open microphone non-destructively
nodes.summary: Open the microphone without cutting traces, removing components, or soldering.
acceptance_criteria: Enclosure is open with PCB(s), battery, microphone capsule, controls, and antenna area accessible.
No intentional electrical modification has been made.
outputs: Accessible hardware for documentation

nodes.title: Document hardware
nodes.summary: Photograph and record the complete hardware before probing.
acceptance_criteria: Clear images of both sides of every PCB are captured.
All readable IC, crystal, regulator, battery, connector, and board markings are recorded.
Microphone capsule wiring, antenna/RF area, charging circuitry, controls, and test pads are visible.
outputs: PCB photo set captured with the internal sled removed and both PCB faces visible.

Connector/component markings documented, including M+/M- microphone connector, B+/B- battery connector, CL4054H charger marking, 24.000 MHz crystal, AC7006-family/JL SoC area, USB-C, PCB antenna, buttons, LEDs/test pads.

nodes.title: Identify parts and functional blocks
nodes.summary: Major functional blocks are identified. The exact JieLi AC7006 suffix/package remains unresolved, so later probing will use board continuity rather than an assumed variant pinout.
acceptance_criteria: Ground and battery connections are identified.
Likely power regulation, charging, microphone front end, DSP/control, RF, and antenna regions are identified.
Candidate IC functions are recorded with confidence/uncertainty.
outputs: Main SoC: JieLi/Jerry AC7006 family (confirmed family; exact suffix/package unresolved).
RF block: integrated AC7006-family radio beside a 24.000 MHz crystal feeding a meandered PCB antenna marked ANT-BLE.
Charging block: USB-C 5 V input and CL4054H single-cell Li-ion charger feeding the B+/B- battery path.
Audio input block: two-wire microphone capsule on the white M+/M- connector; likely microphone analog front end is integrated in or immediately adjacent to the AC7006-family SoC.
User-interface block: four tactile switches plus LED/status circuitry routed to the main SoC.
Known uncertainty: publicly located AC7006D documentation is a different 32-pin variant, so its pin numbers must not be applied directly to this board.

nodes.title: Trace microphone signal path
nodes.summary: Trace from the microphone capsule toward processing and the RF section using visual inspection and continuity measurements before powered probing.
acceptance_criteria: Microphone capsule pins and ground/reference are identified.
At least one plausible downstream audio-path node or bus is identified.
Candidate test points are documented before powered measurements.
outputs: Partial continuity-derived mic input netlist recorded in eworkbench/projects/wireless-mic/mic-input-observed.json.
Provisional U1 chip contact map recorded in eworkbench/projects/wireless-mic/jl-u1-chip.json; the JL-A pad position and exact manufacturer pinout remain unknown.
Next: identify JL-A physical contact and trace C1L downstream with power disconnected.

nodes.title: Choose first audio interface to characterize
nodes.question: Which accessible audio-interface candidate should be characterized first?
nodes.decision_rule: Choose the highest-priority credible candidate: post-DSP analog > processed digital audio > pre-DSP/raw analog. If no credible candidate exists, resolve that blocker first.

options.label: Only pre-DSP/raw analog candidate is practical
No credible audio interface identified yet

nodes.title: Characterize post-DSP analog candidate
nodes.summary: Measure the candidate analog signal while speaking and operating microphone controls.
acceptance_criteria: DC bias and approximate AC amplitude are measured.
Response to speech is observed.
Effects/volume/mute influence is recorded.
The node is judged safe or unsafe for a buffered/conditioned AUX prototype.
outputs: Analog signal characterization

nodes.title: Characterize processed digital audio candidate
nodes.summary: Determine whether the candidate bus is plausibly I2S, PCM, or another digital audio interface and characterize its basic signaling.
acceptance_criteria: Signal voltage levels and line roles are estimated or identified.
Clock/data behavior is observed if suitable test equipment is available.
A practical method to convert or capture the bus for an AUX proof is identified.
outputs: Digital audio bus characterization

nodes.title: Characterize pre-DSP analog candidate
nodes.summary: Measure the raw/pre-DSP microphone signal and determine what amplification or buffering is needed.
acceptance_criteria: DC bias and approximate AC amplitude are measured.
Response to speech is observed.
Required gain/buffering for a line-level proof is estimated.
outputs: Raw analog signal characterization

nodes.title: Resolve unknown interface
nodes.summary: Perform targeted part research and additional tracing/probing only far enough to produce at least one credible audio-interface candidate.
acceptance_criteria: A new candidate interface is documented, or a specific blocker is documented with the next required instrument/component.
outputs: Resolved candidate or explicit blocker

nodes.title: Select Iteration 1 proof interface
nodes.question: Which characterized interface should be used for the first wired audio proof?
nodes.decision_rule: Choose the highest-priority interface that is understood well enough to connect safely: post-DSP analog > processed digital > pre-DSP analog.

options.label: Use characterized digital interface with conversion
Insufficient characterization; define a targeted follow-on node

nodes.title: Build analog conditioning path
nodes.summary: Create the minimum safe buffer/gain/attenuation/coupling needed to feed the selected analog signal toward the M45 AUX input.
acceptance_criteria: Conditioning approach is documented.
Expected output level and DC isolation are checked before connection to M45.
outputs: Temporary analog interface circuit

nodes.title: Build digital-to-analog proof path
nodes.summary: Use available or acquired conversion hardware to turn the selected digital audio interface into a safe analog signal for M45 AUX.
acceptance_criteria: Digital stream is captured/converted well enough to produce analog audio.
Analog output is checked for safe level and DC behavior.
outputs: Temporary digital-audio conversion path

nodes.title: Record Iteration 1 blocker and extend roadmap
nodes.summary: If no interface is yet safe enough for a proof, record the precise blocker and add new DAG nodes rather than forcing a connection.
acceptance_criteria: Blocker is specific and evidence-based.
Required next measurement, tool, component, or research task is represented by new node(s) in todo.json.
outputs: Updated roadmap with targeted follow-on work

nodes.title: Run wired M45 AUX proof
nodes.summary: Connect the conditioned/converted microphone audio to the ON M45 AUX input and test live speech.
acceptance_criteria: Intelligible live microphone audio is reproduced through the M45.
No unsafe heating, clipping, DC behavior, or obvious electrical fault occurs.
outputs: Working wired proof or documented failure

nodes.title: Evaluate audio and control behavior
nodes.summary: Characterize the successful proof well enough to judge it as the Iteration 1 interface.
acceptance_criteria: Intelligibility/noise is assessed.
Available level is assessed.
Volume, echo/effects, and mute behavior at the selected tap are recorded.
The microphone still operates normally enough for continued development.
outputs: Iteration 1 interface evaluation

nodes.title: Iteration 1 exit readiness
nodes.question: Have all Iteration 1 exit criteria been demonstrated?
nodes.decision_rule: Answer yes only when architecture, usable interface, wired M45 proof, control behavior, and Iteration 2 decision inputs are all documented.

options.label: No; add explicit missing-work nodes to this DAG

nodes.title: Select Iteration 2 wireless architecture
nodes.question: Which wireless architecture should follow the proven audio interface?
nodes.decision_rule: Use teardown findings, interface type, latency needs, preservation of effects, available inventory, and implementation effort.

options.label: Preserve original wireless system / compatible receiver
Replace link with custom low-latency wireless bridge
Use Bluetooth bridge if measured latency is acceptable
Choose another architecture revealed by teardown
